column1: # Vocalis latency corpus (see README.md). Format: id<TAB>kind<TAB>text; kind is short or long.
# short: one sentence, at most 15 words (budget: stop -> pasted p50 < 1.0 s, p95 < 2.0 s).
# long: about 150 words, roughly 60 s of speech (budget: stop -> pasted p50 < 3.0 s).
# Lines starting with # are comments. Text is UTF-8 and never contains a tab.

Okay, a few thoughts on this pull request before it goes in. Overall the structure is good, and splitting the parser into smaller functions makes it much easier to follow. My main concern is error handling. Right now, if the config file is missing a field, the code quietly falls back to a default, and the user never finds out. I'd rather we return an error that names the missing field and the line number, so people can fix their file instead of guessing. Second, the retry loop in the network client doesn't have an upper limit. If the server is down for an hour, we'll keep trying forever and fill the log. Let's cap it at five attempts with a growing delay between them. Third, small thing, a couple of the test names describe how the code works rather than what it should do, so they'll be confusing when they fail. None of this is blocking on its own, but I'd like the first two fixed before we merge.

Some ideas I want to remember from my walk this afternoon. The garden needs a better watering plan before summer. Last year the tomatoes did great in June and then half of them split during the heat in July, probably because I watered too much and too late. This year I want to try a simple drip line on a timer, early in the morning, and keep notes every week on what works. Second, I've been meaning to start the reading group again. Maybe once a month, on a Sunday, alternating between fiction and something practical, like history or cooking. I should ask Nadia and Hamid if they're still interested; they were the most regular last time. Third, money. I keep saying I'll put aside a little every month for the new roof, and I keep not doing it. An automatic transfer of two hundred dollars right after payday is probably the only thing that will actually work. Okay, that's enough planning for one day. Time to make dinner.
